title: Affine base change: pushforward of a quasi-coherent module along an affine morphism commutes with arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be an affine morphism of schemes [pqf-def-affine-morphism], $g:S'\to S$ a morphism, $X'=X\times_SS'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to S'$, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. (1) $f_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, and the base change map $g^*f_*\mathcal F\to f'_*(g')^*\mathcal F$ (adjoint [def-pc-module-pullback] to $f_*\mathcal F\to f_*g'_*(g')^*\mathcal F=g_*f'_*(g')^*\mathcal F$) is an isomorphism; over affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq S'$ above $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, with $f^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}R)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $M=\mathcal F(\operatorname{Spec}B)$, it is the identification $R'\otimes_RM=(R'\otimes_RB)\otimes_BM$. (2) For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, composed with $f'_*$ of the isomorphism $(g')^*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_{X'}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf], it is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{S'}$-algebras $g^*f_*\mathcal O_X\cong f'_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ (the algebra structure on $g^*\mathcal A$, $\mathcal A=f_*\mathcal O_X$, induced through $g^*(\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A)\cong g^*\mathcal A\otimes g^*\mathcal A$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] and $g^*\mathcal O_S\cong\mathcal O_{S'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]). (3) The base change maps are compatible with composition: for a further $h:S''\to S'$, the base change map for $g\circ h$ equals the composite of $h^*$ of the one for $g$ with the one for $h$ (applied to $f'$ and $(g')^*\mathcal F$), under $(g\circ h)^*=h^*g^*$ and $(g'\circ h')^*=h'^*g'^*$ (the composition isomorphisms of [def-pc-module-pullback]), where $X''=X'\times_{S'}S''$ is identified with $X\times_SS''$ with projection $g'\circ h'$ [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KG (lemma-affine-base-change) and the base change diagram (equation-base-change-diagram) before it; (2) and (3) are not stated by Stacks: (2) is the affine-local formula of (1) for M = B, which is a ring isomorphism R' (x)_R B = R' (x)_R B; (3) follows from the same local formula

proof.text: *Step 1 (quasi-coherence of $f_*\mathcal F$).* An affine morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) (with the definition [pqf-def-affine-morphism]), so $f_*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] (Schemes, Lemma 01LC). (On an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$ with $f^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}B$ it is $\widetilde{M_R}$, $M=\mathcal F(f^{-1}U)$, by Step 4.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KG, statement ('$f_*\mathcal F$ is a quasi-coherent sheaf'); the proof's first sentence cites relative affine vanishing (02KE) for $Rf_*$, which is not part of this node; quasi-coherence is Schemes, Lemma 01LC

proof.text: *Step 2 (the question is local on $S$ and $S'$).* Let $\beta_{\mathcal F}:g^*f_*\mathcal F\to f'_*g'^*\mathcal F$ be the base change map of the statement (it is the base change map in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction] for the square $(f,f',g,g')$). For every point $s'\in S'$ choose an affine open $U\subseteq S$ containing $g(s')$ and an affine open $V\subseteq g^{-1}(U)$ containing $s'$ [def-pc-scheme]. Put $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$, affine because $f$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $X'_V=f'^{-1}(V)$; since $f(g'(x'))=g(f'(x'))\in U$ for $x'\in X'_V$, $g'(X'_V)\subseteq X_U$, and the restrictions $f_U:X_U\to U$, $f'_V:X'_V\to V$, $g_V:V\to U$, $g'_V:X'_V\to X_U$ form a commutative square. It is cartesian: by [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] applied to $X'=X\times_SS'$ and the opens $X_U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq S'$, $U\subseteq S$, the fibre product $X_U\times_UV$ is the open subscheme $g'^{-1}(X_U)\cap f'^{-1}(V)=f'^{-1}(V)=X'_V$ with the restricted projections. The inclusions $j_U,j_V,j_X,j_{X'}$ are open immersions satisfying the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction] ($j_X(X_U)=f^{-1}(U)$, $j_{X'}(X'_V)=f'^{-1}(V)$), so $j_V^*(\beta_{\mathcal F})$ is an isomorphism if and only if the base change map $\beta^{\circ}_{j_X^*\mathcal F}$ of the restricted square is. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] $j_V^*\cong(-)|_V$ naturally, so $j_V^*(\beta_{\mathcal F})$ is an isomorphism iff $\beta_{\mathcal F}|_V$ is, and $j_X^*\mathcal F\cong\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2). Suppose (Steps 3, 4) that $\beta^{\circ}$ is an isomorphism for every such restricted square. Then $\beta_{\mathcal F}(W)$ is bijective for every open $W$ contained in one of the chosen $V$; these $W$ form a basis of the topology of $S'$, so $\beta_{\mathcal F}$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis](b). So it suffices to treat a cartesian square with $S$, $S'$, $X$ affine and $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KG, proof, first sentence: 'The statement is local on $S$ and $S'$. Hence we may assume ...' (the locality argument is written out here)

proof.text: *Step 3 (spectra).* Let $S$, $S'$, $X$ be affine and $X'$ a fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]; put $R=\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$, $R'=\Gamma(S',\mathcal O_{S'})$, $B=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and let $\varphi=f^\sharp:R\to B$, $\psi=g^\sharp:R\to R'$ be the ring maps on global sections. The canonical morphisms $S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $S'\to\operatorname{Spec}R'$, $X\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ (corresponding to the identities of the rings) are isomorphisms since the schemes are affine, and under them $f$ and $g$ become $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Spec}\psi$ [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] $\operatorname{Spec}R'\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}B\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_RB)$ with projections $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, so by uniqueness of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] there is an isomorphism $X'\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_RB)$ compatible with the projections. Isomorphisms of schemes are open immersions, so [lem-weil-pbc-module-base-change-map-open-restriction] (with these isomorphisms as $j_U,j_V,j_X,j_{X'}$; the preimage conditions hold trivially) identifies $\beta_{\mathcal F}$, up to the isomorphisms $a,b$ there, with the base change map of the square $f=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}\psi$, $g'=\operatorname{Spec}(b\mapsto1\otimes b)$, $f'=\operatorname{Spec}(r'\mapsto r'\otimes1)$ on $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_RB)$, applied to the pullback of $\mathcal F$ along the isomorphism, which is quasi-coherent ([lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2)). So we may assume this square of spectra.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 02KG, proof: 'we may assume $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}(R')$ ... $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(R'\otimes_RA)$' (Schemes, Lemma 01JQ/01I4 for the fibre product)

proof.text: *Step 4 (the affine computation, part (1)).* In the square of Step 3 let $M=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,\mathcal F)$. Since $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, the counit $\widetilde M\to\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3), so by naturality of $\beta$ we may assume $\mathcal F=\widetilde M$. Put $P=(R'\otimes_RB)\otimes_BM$, an $R'$-module through $r'\mapsto r'\otimes1$. We have isomorphisms: $\pi:f_*\widetilde M\cong\widetilde{M_R}$ with $\pi(\tau_B(m))=\tau_R(m)$ and $\pi':f'_*\widetilde P\cong\widetilde{P_{R'}}$ with $\pi'(\tau(p))=\tau(p)$ [lem-weil-pbc-pushforward-tilde-spec]; $\theta:g^*\widetilde{M_R}\cong\widetilde{R'\otimes_RM}$ with $\theta(\eta_g(\tau_R(m)))=\tau(1\otimes m)$ and $\theta':g'^*\widetilde M\cong\widetilde P$ with $\theta'(\eta_{g'}(\tau_B(m)))=\tau((1\otimes1)\otimes m)$ [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change]. Let $\tilde\beta=\pi'\circ f'_*(\theta')\circ\beta_{\widetilde M}\circ g^*(\pi)^{-1}\circ\theta^{-1}:\widetilde{R'\otimes_RM}\to\widetilde{P_{R'}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1),(2) ($\tau$ is an isomorphism on global sections and $\alpha\mapsto\alpha_X\circ\tau$ is bijective) $\tilde\beta=\widetilde u$ for the $R'$-linear map $u:R'\otimes_RM\to P$ determined by $\tilde\beta(\tau(x))=\tau(u(x))$. Compute $u(1\otimes m)$: $\tau(1\otimes m)=\theta(\eta_g(\tau_R(m)))=\theta(g^*(\pi)(\eta_g(s)))$ with $s=\tau_B(m)\in\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,f_*\widetilde M)$, by naturality of the unit $\eta_g$. By the definition of $\beta$ as the adjoint of $f_*(\eta_{g'})$, $g_*(\beta)\circ\eta_{g,f_*\widetilde M}=f_*(\eta_{g',\widetilde M})$, i.e. $\beta(\eta_g(s))=\eta_{g'}(\tau_B(m))\in\Gamma(X',g'^*\widetilde M)=\Gamma(S',f'_*g'^*\widetilde M)$. Hence $\tilde\beta(\tau(1\otimes m))=\pi'(\theta'(\eta_{g'}(\tau_B(m))))=\tau((1\otimes1)\otimes m)$, so $u(1\otimes m)=(1\otimes1)\otimes m$ and, by $R'$-linearity, $u(r'\otimes m)=(r'\otimes1)\otimes m$. This $u$ is the canonical isomorphism $R'\otimes_RM\cong(R'\otimes_RB)\otimes_BM$, with inverse $(r'\otimes b)\otimes m\mapsto r'\otimes bm$ (well defined: $(r'\otimes b)\mapsto(m\mapsto r'\otimes bm)$ is $R$-balanced in $(r',b)$ and the result is $B$-balanced; the two composites are the identity on generators). So $\tilde\beta=\widetilde u$ is an isomorphism (a functor preserves isomorphisms), hence so is $\beta_{\widetilde M}$. With Step 2 this proves (1), and identifies $\beta$ over $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subseteq S'$ above $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with $R'\otimes_RM=(R'\otimes_RB)\otimes_BM$.
